title: M5: Google sign-in (Cognito) and abuse protection
description: Intent: As a student, I want to sign in with my Google account, so that I can use the IDE from anywhere without a new password; as the maintainer, I want only approved students able to start sessions, so that strangers cannot run code or run up the bill. Includes: Google Cloud project and OAuth client (set up together with the maintainer), Cognito user pool with Google as federated identity provider and hosted UI, allowlist of approved Google accounts enforced by a pre-sign-up Lambda trigger, JWT verification on the control and proxy endpoints, per-session token, limits on concurrent sessions and session length, AWS Budget alarm. Excludes: password or other social logins, self-service signup by unapproved accounts. DoD: an approved Google account signs in and starts a session; an unapproved account is refused; unauthenticated requests get 401; a second concurrent session per student is refused; budget alarm exists.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Google side done: Google Cloud project and Web OAuth client created, redirect URI https://sierrendipity.auth.us-east-1.amazoncognito.com/oauth2/idpresponse, credentials stored in Secrets Manager (us-east-1, legacy account) as sierrendipity/google-oauth. Remaining for the maintainer: add the student's Google email as a test user on the Audience page. Cognito domain prefix sierrendipity was free as of today. Implementation waits on the M4 stack.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Design constraint from the maintainer: no email addresses in code, specs, fixtures, docs, or the board. The sign-in allowlist lives outside the repo (an SSM SecureString or Secrets Manager value created by the maintainer), the pre-sign-up Lambda reads it at runtime, and Gherkin specs use generated placeholder identities.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Deployed (Cognito domain sierrendipity, Google OAuth configured); authorize redirects to Google. Waiting on a real Google sign-in.

right_now_summary: Google sign-in and allowlist checks are deployed; tests for refusal, sign-out, and extra sessions remain.
